note: Acceptance seed only. Presence grants no completion credit. Expand scope, evidence, estimates, dependencies and platform applicability before advancing stages.

items.title: Identify the authorized workstation
items.acceptanceSeed: Match the discovered device to the intended MTerm host before any mutation.

items.title: Verify local source write access
items.acceptanceSeed: A new ignored file survives create, read-back, rename and second read-back.

items.title: Separate GitHub capabilities
items.acceptanceSeed: Record branch/content/workflow writes, CI, merges and tags as separately verified or untested.

items.title: Check current repository identity
items.acceptanceSeed: Confirm the exact owner/repository, default branch and local remote URL.

items.title: Inventory dirty and untracked work
items.acceptanceSeed: Every pre-existing staged, unstaged or untracked item is preserved or explicitly classified.

items.title: Inventory published heads and open PRs
items.acceptanceSeed: Record current hashes and distinguish unique work from integrated ancestry.

items.title: Exclude access probes from product merges
items.acceptanceSeed: The access-check branch and disabled permission-test workflow do not enter product history.

items.title: Preserve local recovery-only branches
items.acceptanceSeed: Local CI/history archives remain recoverable without installing unauthorized content.

items.title: Create a pre-change source checkpoint
items.acceptanceSeed: Verify the source manifest and Git bundle, with sensitive/ignored exclusions documented.

items.title: Resolve content conflicts deliberately
items.acceptanceSeed: Each true conflict receives a reviewed resolution, not a whole-tree local/remote overwrite.

items.title: Establish a verified publication baseline
items.acceptanceSeed: Remote main and the local integration baseline have recorded, reconciled hashes/trees.

items.title: Record recovery and outstanding process state
items.acceptanceSeed: A later session can identify the first unverified action without replaying completed mutations.

items.title: Create the legacy-to-GUI export map
items.acceptanceSeed: The map accounts for every GUI source, configuration, test and documentation path exported from legacy MTerm to MTerm-GUI.

items.title: Preserve legacy GUI Git history
items.acceptanceSeed: The legacy GUI commit graph and required product refs remain recoverable in MTerm-GUI or the verified pre-split bundle.

items.title: Preserve GUI automation in MTerm-GUI root
items.acceptanceSeed: GUI workflows live under MTerm-GUI/.github/workflows; CLI workflows live independently under MTerm-CLI/.github/workflows.

items.title: Preserve GUI contributor entry points and add CLI equivalents
items.acceptanceSeed: Each repository's root instructions route work to that product and cross-link the sibling repository without duplicated mutable rules.

items.title: Export native GUI source to MTerm-GUI
items.acceptanceSeed: The same native features remain buildable from MTerm-GUI/native after repository export.

items.title: Preserve the Electron reference in MTerm-GUI
items.acceptanceSeed: The reference source, tests and dependency lock remain runnable in MTerm-GUI.

items.title: Isolate CLI from GUI package dependencies
items.acceptanceSeed: MTerm-CLI installation does not transitively install packages from MTerm-GUI or Electron/Qt.

items.title: Verify native CMake paths in the MTerm-GUI checkout
items.acceptanceSeed: Fresh configure/build succeeds without depending on the old source/build directory.

items.title: Verify PowerShell and GUI launchers in MTerm-GUI
items.acceptanceSeed: Native build/package/start commands resolve the new product root correctly.

items.title: Verify GUI-reference test and fixture paths after export
items.acceptanceSeed: Reference tests execute against the relocated source, not stale previous builds.

items.title: Preserve GUI roadmap identity and scope
items.acceptanceSeed: IDs, baseline weights and requirement text survive migration without artificial credit.

items.title: Correct GUI evidence references
items.acceptanceSeed: Every live evidence path resolves after relocation; historical provenance stays attributable.

items.title: Verify GUI source-fingerprint coverage in MTerm-GUI
items.acceptanceSeed: Changing MTerm-GUI/native or its GUI reference source demonstrably invalidates an unreviewed GUI metric snapshot.

items.title: Preserve checkpoints and ignored user state
items.acceptanceSeed: No auth, profile, old checkout, artifact or active toolchain is swept into a bulk move.

items.title: Recreate path-sensitive caches safely
items.acceptanceSeed: New CMake/Python/Node development state is tested while old recoverable state is retained.

items.title: Keep compatible desktop launching
items.acceptanceSeed: A documented old entry point forwards correctly or has a clearly tested replacement.

items.title: Verify unchanged GUI behavior
items.acceptanceSeed: Native/reference gates run; relocation-only edits do not redesign GUI business behavior.

items.title: Keep GUI business work independent after export
items.acceptanceSeed: Later CLI commits contain no unrelated GUI changes; necessary path fixes are separately justified.

items.title: Inspect all three actual upstream projects
items.acceptanceSeed: Read manifests, source entry points, auth, lifecycle and licensing at recorded commits.

items.title: Document the native Codex boundary
items.acceptanceSeed: The adapter invokes Codex as a native binary rather than assuming JavaScript internals.

items.title: Select a supported Node LTS for MTerm glue
items.acceptanceSeed: Verify lifecycle support and pin/test the selected Node line and patch policy.

items.title: Determine the Web runtime dependency set
items.acceptanceSeed: Identify Bun, Electron/browser and bridge/helper requirements from the selected upstream pin.

items.title: Resolve the no-daemon constraint
items.acceptanceSeed: Prove compliant operation or record the exact session-helper/persistent-service deviation for approval.

items.title: Resolve the no-GUI constraint
items.acceptanceSeed: Do not ship a desktop launcher inside the purported pure CLI without an explicit approved exception.

items.title: Resolve the single-runtime constraint
items.acceptanceSeed: Report extra upstream runtimes separately; a compiled helper is not mislabeled pure Node.

items.title: Resolve the under-50-MB constraint
items.acceptanceSeed: Measure all required installed payloads and leave the requirement blocked if they exceed the budget.

items.title: Keep the three-integration scope visible
items.acceptanceSeed: Core-only progress never silently excludes the desired Web integration from completion accounting.

items.title: Record module and lifecycle ownership
items.acceptanceSeed: Each adapter has a narrow contract, owner, cancellation policy and bounded resources.

items.acceptanceSeed: The installed/link-created command invokes the real CLI from outside the checkout.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Make help work offline
items.acceptanceSeed: Help succeeds without credentials, dependencies installed, network or model calls.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Make version output deterministic
items.acceptanceSeed: Version identifies MTerm CLI independently of the GUI and can report pinned components safely.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Dispatch the required subcommands
items.acceptanceSeed: Status, update and config route correctly without being forwarded accidentally to Codex.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Support explicit Codex argument passthrough
items.acceptanceSeed: Arguments following -- reach Codex byte/argument-equivalently without shell evaluation.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Preserve the caller working directory
items.acceptanceSeed: Launch tests show Codex sees the requested caller workspace rather than the install directory.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Handle paths with spaces and Unicode
items.acceptanceSeed: Launch and config paths work without quoting loss or command injection.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Preserve inherited terminal I/O
items.acceptanceSeed: The actual agent gets interactive stdin/stdout/stderr where appropriate, not captured fake TUI output.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Propagate interrupts and shutdown
items.acceptanceSeed: Ctrl+C and relevant signals reach the intended child and restore terminal state.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Preserve child exit outcomes
items.acceptanceSeed: Codex failures/cancellation are not converted into a misleading MTerm success exit.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Avoid unsolicited startup work
items.acceptanceSeed: Ordinary launches do not update, install, query quotas or silently reconfigure credentials.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Define non-interactive semantics
items.acceptanceSeed: Pipes and redirected input do not hang on hidden confirmation prompts.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Reject unknown wrapper flags safely
items.acceptanceSeed: Wrapper errors are explicit while passthrough arguments remain available after the delimiter.

items.section: Entry point and CLI argument behavior
items.title: Avoid executable recursion/collisions
items.acceptanceSeed: Resolving codex never resolves mterm-cli back to itself or replaces an unrelated installation.

items.title: Resolve exact Codex version and artifact
items.acceptanceSeed: The manifest names a real source commit and the corresponding platform distribution.

items.title: Verify Codex download integrity
items.acceptanceSeed: Hash/signature checks use reviewed provenance and reject a modified artifact.

items.title: Select only the current platform payload
items.acceptanceSeed: A production install does not carry every operating system and architecture binary.

items.title: Support an explicitly selected existing Codex
items.acceptanceSeed: External-binary mode validates compatibility and labels itself dependency-reuse, not self-contained.

items.title: Preserve Codex configuration precedence
items.acceptanceSeed: The wrapper respects supported CODEX_HOME/config behavior without silently overriding user settings.

items.title: Preserve Codex safety approvals
items.acceptanceSeed: No approval-bypass or sandbox-weakening flags are automatically added.

items.title: Test actual upstream executable startup
items.acceptanceSeed: Allowed non-model probes verify real binary launch in addition to deterministic child fixtures.

items.title: Diagnose missing/incompatible executables
items.acceptanceSeed: Errors distinguish absence, wrong architecture, unsupported version and execution failure.

items.title: Preserve resumable session behavior
items.acceptanceSeed: Documented Codex resume arguments pass through without relocating or corrupting its history.

items.title: Avoid persistent agent processes by default
items.acceptanceSeed: No resident service remains merely because help, config or status was used.

items.title: Pin the Web adapter and compatibility contract
items.acceptanceSeed: Record the actual commit/version and compatible Codex route/model contract.

items.title: Verify a genuine non-GUI integration path
items.acceptanceSeed: Exercise a supported path or record why the selected upstream requires an approved companion.

items.title: Keep one-time setup explicit
items.acceptanceSeed: Initial browser/session/connector setup has a named entry point and clear human actions.

items.title: Reuse supported existing Web sessions
items.acceptanceSeed: Reuse is limited to upstream-supported owned profiles, not cookie extraction or arbitrary session copying.

items.title: Distinguish Web and Codex auth readiness
items.acceptanceSeed: Doctor/config do not treat auth.json presence as a browser login.

items.title: Verify real model discovery
items.acceptanceSeed: Model availability is sourced from the configured account/integration, not a hardcoded marketing list.

items.title: Make configured Web routes available in Codex
items.acceptanceSeed: Test the actual picker/catalog path under the compatible upstream protocol.

items.title: Prevent silent transport/model fallback
items.acceptanceSeed: An unavailable selected Web model fails clearly instead of secretly using native/API quota.

items.title: Preserve model identity and supported effort
items.acceptanceSeed: Do not translate effort/model settings through guessed undocumented flags.

items.title: Protect existing model routes
items.acceptanceSeed: Any required config integration is scoped, backed up and conflict-checked before mutation.

items.title: Restore only owned route changes
items.acceptanceSeed: Disable/rollback restores MTerm-owned settings without undoing unrelated user changes.

items.title: Own any approved session helper lifetime
items.acceptanceSeed: Start/stop only helpers belonging to the MTerm session, with explicit version and health checks.

items.title: Do not install background autostart
items.acceptanceSeed: No login item, scheduled task, system service or persistent daemon is enabled without separate approval.

items.title: Handle browser/selector drift explicitly
items.acceptanceSeed: Changed upstream behavior yields a diagnosed failure, not repeated submissions or guessed results.

items.title: Handle interrupted Web sessions safely
items.acceptanceSeed: Cancellation avoids duplicate submissions and leaves owned helper/session state understandable.

items.title: Keep Codex quota distinct from Web allowances
items.acceptanceSeed: Usage labels never claim that pi-codex-status is a Web/Pro message counter.

items.title: Gate live Web acceptance on authorization
items.acceptanceSeed: An account-bound smoke is opt-in, records actual behavior and never exposes credentials.

items.title: Keep incompatible Web acceptance blocked
items.acceptanceSeed: No final all-three-components completion claim while required runtime/auth/size conflicts remain unresolved.

items.title: Default quota auth to Codex
items.acceptanceSeed: The upstream auto preference cannot silently select MultiCodex or pi accounts.

items.title: Honor an explicit auth-file path
items.acceptanceSeed: The requested source is resolved safely without falling back to unrelated accounts.

items.title: Honor supported CODEX_HOME behavior
items.acceptanceSeed: An alternate Codex home is handled through an explicit adapter path when upstream lacks support.

items.title: Handle missing credentials
items.acceptanceSeed: Show actionable existing-login guidance without creating a new MTerm account.

items.title: Handle malformed credentials
items.acceptanceSeed: Invalid JSON/types fail safely and do not produce partial token-bearing diagnostics.

items.title: Handle API-key versus OAuth mode
items.acceptanceSeed: Unsupported quota data is marked unavailable rather than fabricating OAuth usage.

items.title: Handle OS keyring credentials honestly
items.acceptanceSeed: Unsupported keyring access is reported; credentials are never exported to plaintext for convenience.

items.title: Keep credentials out of process arguments
items.acceptanceSeed: Bearer/refresh tokens and cookies never appear in argv or diagnostic command examples.

items.title: Keep credentials out of logs and stdout
items.acceptanceSeed: All success/error paths are tested with sentinel secrets absent from output.

items.title: Keep credentials out of repository artifacts
items.acceptanceSeed: Staging, snapshots, issue bodies and CI uploads exclude real credential material.

items.title: Identify token-refresh side effects
items.acceptanceSeed: Document whether the pinned status adapter can write the shared auth source.

items.title: Bound refresh timeout/retries
items.acceptanceSeed: A refresh failure cannot hang a status command or repeatedly rotate tokens.

items.title: Protect concurrent credential updates
items.acceptanceSeed: Test account changes and unrelated field edits; use coordinated or fail-closed behavior.

items.title: Preserve credential file protection
items.acceptanceSeed: Legitimate authorized refresh maintains owner-only protection and existing unrelated fields.

items.title: Distinguish app-local locks from external coordination
items.acceptanceSeed: Do not claim that an MTerm lock serializes an unrelated Codex process.

items.title: Prevent statusline auth mutation
items.acceptanceSeed: The default prompt-hook path cannot quietly refresh credentials or initiate sign-in.

items.title: Avoid account details in public output
items.acceptanceSeed: Email/account identifiers are omitted or pseudonymized unless explicitly requested and safe.

items.title: Handle revoked/expired auth without evasion
items.acceptanceSeed: Report the required human upstream reauthentication; do not switch identities to escape limits.

items.title: Integrate the real pi status surface
items.acceptanceSeed: The wrapper calls verified library/CLI behavior, not a replacement hardcoded success report.

items.title: Recognize private endpoint instability
items.acceptanceSeed: The implementation documents and distinguishes schema drift and unsupported responses.

items.title: Preserve source window durations
items.acceptanceSeed: Window duration remains source-driven in seconds rather than always assuming two fixed periods.

items.title: Normalize used and remaining percentages
items.acceptanceSeed: Test supported values, bounds, missing values and semantics without silently clamping away errors.

items.title: Preserve reset timestamp units
items.acceptanceSeed: Unix seconds and milliseconds are handled explicitly and normalized consistently.

items.title: Render local reset times safely
items.acceptanceSeed: Local display and UTC machine timestamps agree, including daylight-saving boundaries.

items.title: Distinguish missing versus zero quota
items.acceptanceSeed: Null/unknown data cannot be displayed as exhausted or fully available.

items.title: Normalize credits without invention
items.acceptanceSeed: Known balance, unknown balance and source-supported unlimited state remain distinct.

items.title: Preserve additional named limits
items.acceptanceSeed: Per-model or named limits are carried through with bounded safe labels.

items.title: Return meaningful service errors
items.acceptanceSeed: 401,403,429,timeout,offline and server failures have distinct tested diagnoses.

items.title: Respect retry guidance and rate limits
items.acceptanceSeed: Bounded retries honor Retry-After and do not hammer private endpoints.

items.title: Avoid model calls for usage inspection
items.acceptanceSeed: Status tests assert that no coding completion or Web message is sent.

items.title: Prevent credential-bearing origin changes
items.acceptanceSeed: Endpoint overrides and redirects cannot send real tokens to an arbitrary host.

items.title: Bound response size and parsing
items.acceptanceSeed: Oversized/malformed upstream responses are rejected with sanitized error output.

items.title: Render the requested boxed status
items.acceptanceSeed: The normal terminal view shows supported quota/credits/resets in a readable box.

items.title: Render a single compact status line
items.acceptanceSeed: The --line mode emits one bounded line, not spinners or multiline diagnostics.

items.title: Produce versioned JSON-only stdout
items.acceptanceSeed: The --json path emits exactly one parseable document on success and expected errors.

items.title: Use stable structured error codes
items.acceptanceSeed: Consumers do not need to scrape human error strings to distinguish failure modes.

items.title: Expose freshness in every format
items.acceptanceSeed: Fresh, cached, stale and unavailable values remain distinguishable.

items.title: Support NO_COLOR and dumb terminals
items.acceptanceSeed: No-color/plain modes avoid ANSI escapes and unsuitable Unicode decoration.

items.title: Handle narrow display widths
items.acceptanceSeed: Clipping/wrapping remains readable and does not corrupt the terminal.

items.title: Sanitize untrusted terminal controls
items.acceptanceSeed: Upstream labels/errors cannot inject CSI/OSC hyperlinks, titles or escape sequences.

items.title: Preserve shell/tmux prompt safety
items.acceptanceSeed: Status text does not execute or inject prompt-language syntax through unescaped values.

items.title: Define quota-exhausted exit semantics
items.acceptanceSeed: A valid exhausted quota result is not mistaken for network or parser failure.

items.title: Keep raw secret-bearing data private
items.acceptanceSeed: Normalized output never includes auth documents or unfiltered HTTP error bodies.

items.title: Keep output deterministic under fixtures
items.acceptanceSeed: Stable snapshots cover time/locale-sensitive output with controlled clocks and settings.

items.title: Use a per-user cache location
items.acceptanceSeed: Platform paths are documented and isolated from GUI state and source checkout.

items.title: Bind cache to the selected account/source
items.acceptanceSeed: Switching accounts cannot display a previous account’s quota.

items.title: Define cache schema and size bounds
items.acceptanceSeed: Unknown schema/corrupt/oversized cache fails safely without unbounded reads.

items.title: Write cache atomically
items.acceptanceSeed: Interrupted writes do not destroy the last usable snapshot.

items.title: Test concurrent readers and writers
items.acceptanceSeed: Contention produces coherent snapshots, not partial JSON or silent cross-account merges.

items.title: Implement explicit TTL behavior
items.acceptanceSeed: Freshness is deterministic under a controlled clock.

items.title: Handle future clock/skew cases
items.acceptanceSeed: A future timestamp does not become indefinitely fresh.

items.title: Handle cache directory permission errors
items.acceptanceSeed: Status can report the problem without changing broad filesystem permissions.

items.title: Offer clearly labeled stale fallback
items.acceptanceSeed: Network failure may reuse an allowed stale result only with visible staleness.

items.title: Keep statusline bounded and offline by default
items.acceptanceSeed: A prompt hook does not wait for a remote request or create a background worker.

items.title: Implement effective config display
items.acceptanceSeed: Show non-secret values and precedence sources, not raw auth.

items.title: Implement typed config get/set
items.acceptanceSeed: Unsupported keys and wrong types are rejected before mutation.

items.title: Implement safe config editing
items.acceptanceSeed: An invalid editor result preserves the previous validated configuration.

items.title: Version config schemas
items.acceptanceSeed: Migrations preserve existing values and are tested against representative old files.

items.title: Use atomic config writes and backups
items.acceptanceSeed: A failed write/migration does not strand the installed CLI.

items.title: Reject prototype-pollution keys
items.acceptanceSeed: Merging configuration cannot alter object prototypes or runtime behavior through inherited properties.

items.title: Resolve config/data/cache paths explicitly
items.acceptanceSeed: Flags/environment/default precedence is documented and tested.

items.title: Provide offline doctor output
items.acceptanceSeed: Dependency/auth-source/config/cache readiness is diagnosed without real token or model calls.

items.title: Provide structured doctor JSON
items.acceptanceSeed: Missing, unsupported, blocked and ready states are stable machine-readable values.

items.title: Keep network diagnostics opt-in
items.acceptanceSeed: A health check requiring network is clearly separate from ordinary help/config inspection.

items.title: Create immutable versions.json records
items.acceptanceSeed: Each required component has an exact source commit and distribution identity.

items.title: Record platform asset checksums
items.acceptanceSeed: Downloads can be checked against a trusted reviewed manifest.

items.title: Commit a coherent CLI package lock
items.acceptanceSeed: Clean installs reproduce the same declared production dependency graph.

items.title: Record the compatible three-component set
items.acceptanceSeed: Pins are tested as a combination, not independently assumed compatible.

items.title: Choose a maintainable vendor strategy
items.acceptanceSeed: Submodule/subtree/snapshot initialization and update behavior work from a clean clone.

items.title: Preserve upstream notices and licenses
items.acceptanceSeed: Vendored code retains its original licenses and attribution.

items.title: Track patches separately
items.acceptanceSeed: Every patch has rationale, hash, upstream base and regression evidence.

items.title: Detect upstream patch drift
items.acceptanceSeed: An update refuses to silently apply a patch to incompatible source.

items.title: Avoid shipping full upstream development histories
items.acceptanceSeed: The runtime package excludes repositories/toolchains/tests not required to execute.

items.title: Separate desired pins from installed state
items.acceptanceSeed: The installed manifest records exact active versions without rewriting source pins.

items.title: Implement non-mutating update check
items.acceptanceSeed: --check reports available/reviewed differences without changing installed state or auth.

items.title: Display old-to-new changes before apply
items.acceptanceSeed: The user sees components, hashes, compatibility and footprint implications.

items.title: Require deliberate update confirmation
items.acceptanceSeed: Interactive confirmation or explicit non-interactive --yes is required for mutation.

items.title: Avoid automatic startup updates
items.acceptanceSeed: Default launch/status/config do not call update or schedule it.

items.title: Use a scoped update lock
items.acceptanceSeed: Concurrent updaters cannot activate conflicting versions.

items.title: Validate stale lock ownership
items.acceptanceSeed: Recovery does not kill unrelated processes or delete unrelated lock paths.

items.title: Stage into a new owned directory
items.acceptanceSeed: The active installation remains untouched during download/build/test.

items.title: Bound download time and size
items.acceptanceSeed: A hanging or oversized artifact cannot consume unlimited resources.

items.title: Verify hashes before execution/extraction
items.acceptanceSeed: Untrusted or modified binaries/scripts are never executed.

items.title: Reject archive traversal and link escapes
items.acceptanceSeed: Absolute entries, parent traversal and unsafe symlink/hardlink targets fail safely.

items.title: Reject decompression bombs
items.acceptanceSeed: Extraction enforces file count and expanded-byte budgets.

items.title: Run compatibility checks before activation
items.acceptanceSeed: Failed build/tests/smokes leave the previous version selected.

items.title: Activate atomically
items.acceptanceSeed: The command sees either the old or new coherent component set, not a partial mixture.

items.title: Support exact manifest rollback
items.acceptanceSeed: Rollback selects a known previous owned version without disturbing user state.

items.title: Preserve active sessions during updates
items.acceptanceSeed: Versioned binaries are not removed or replaced beneath running jobs.

items.title: Preserve config/auth/cache/browser profiles
items.acceptanceSeed: An update never resets account login or deletes private state.

items.title: Protect linked developer checkouts
items.acceptanceSeed: Installed-user update logic cannot git-reset or overwrite source/vendor edits.

items.title: Keep update.sh a thin wrapper
items.acceptanceSeed: Shell and CLI entry points call the same tested update engine.

items.title: Implement MTerm-CLI repository-root npm link
items.acceptanceSeed: A clean install from MTerm-CLI repository root exposes mterm-cli without cloning/installing MTerm-GUI.

items.title: Resolve symlinked entry paths
items.acceptanceSeed: Linked commands find their own package/resources outside the current working directory.

items.title: Isolate global test links
items.acceptanceSeed: Test install/uninstall uses an owned temporary prefix and preserves unrelated commands.

items.title: Inspect the real packed tarball
items.acceptanceSeed: Unpack the produced package and assert its complete file allowlist.

items.title: Exclude private and development material
items.acceptanceSeed: No credentials, browser profiles, raw chats, source maps without reason or caches enter distribution.

items.title: Exclude GUI/runtime bloat
items.acceptanceSeed: The CLI dependency/install graph contains no Qt/Electron/GUI code unless explicitly approved as a separate mode.

items.title: Record all production dependency bytes
items.acceptanceSeed: The size report counts target binaries, transitive modules and mandatory side-downloads.

items.title: Separate compressed and installed size
items.acceptanceSeed: The under-50-MB claim uses extracted bytes, not archive compression.

items.title: Label preinstalled prerequisite mode
items.acceptanceSeed: Reusing Node/Codex/companion installations is not presented as a self-contained bundle.

items.title: Provide safe optional installer semantics
items.acceptanceSeed: A bootstrap verifies pinned artifacts, avoids sudo/autostart and preserves shell configuration.

items.title: Version the CLI separately
items.acceptanceSeed: MTerm GUI 0.2.0 and future versions are not overwritten by CLI 0.1.0.

items.title: Diagnose unsupported runtime/platform installs
items.acceptanceSeed: Errors identify required architecture/OS/runtime instead of partially installing.

items.acceptanceSeed: Run the actual supported artifact on an arm64 macOS environment.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Validate macOS x86-64 execution
items.acceptanceSeed: Run the actual Intel artifact rather than assuming arm64 results cover it.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Validate Linux x86-64 execution
items.acceptanceSeed: Declare and test the supported libc/distribution floor and executable permissions.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Assess Linux arm64 explicitly
items.acceptanceSeed: Record whether the full chosen upstream set is supported and tested, or keep it out of claimed support.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Preserve Windows development capability
items.acceptanceSeed: Build/test scripts work on the actual workstation without assuming Unix shell availability.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Verify actual runner architecture
items.acceptanceSeed: CI records process OS/architecture; moving runner labels are not assumed equivalent.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Test interactive terminal integration
items.acceptanceSeed: TTY detection, resize, interrupts and exit restoration work under representative terminals.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Test redirected/non-TTY invocation
items.acceptanceSeed: Commands have documented behavior under pipes, files and CI.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Test cancellation and descendant cleanup
items.acceptanceSeed: Owned session helpers stop without killing unrelated user processes.

items.section: Platform support and native terminal behavior
items.title: Document untested platform boundaries
items.acceptanceSeed: Unsupported/skipped coverage cannot be presented as a passing support matrix.

items.title: Use minimal operation permissions
items.acceptanceSeed: Local file/network/process capabilities are separated and no global settings are widened.

items.title: Keep Codex safety controls intact
items.acceptanceSeed: MTerm never installs automatic approval bypasses for convenience.

items.title: Validate executable and managed-install paths
items.acceptanceSeed: Untrusted config cannot redirect updates or execution outside owned/trusted locations silently.

items.title: Sanitize diagnostics consistently
items.acceptanceSeed: Sentinel credentials are absent from normal errors, debug logs and support reports.

items.title: Restrict credential-bearing endpoint origins
items.acceptanceSeed: Arbitrary endpoints/redirects cannot receive auth headers.

items.title: Reject insecure TLS behavior
items.acceptanceSeed: No insecure TLS flags or certificate-validation disablement are added.

items.title: Prevent silent quota evasion
items.acceptanceSeed: No account switching, route fallback or repeated submission is used to avoid product limits.

items.title: Keep browser access legitimate
items.acceptanceSeed: No session theft, cookie export, CAPTCHA bypass or unsupported privilege escalation.

items.title: Keep default operation daemon-free
items.acceptanceSeed: No persistent updater/status worker/listener or OS startup registration is installed.

items.title: Separate fixture and real credentials
items.acceptanceSeed: Fixture endpoints/modes cannot read the real user auth home.

items.title: Create the root CLI workflow
items.acceptanceSeed: The actual .github/workflows/cli-ci.yml is present and readable on the intended branch.

items.title: Pin workflow actions and permissions
items.acceptanceSeed: Third-party action refs and least-privilege settings are reviewed.

items.title: Run credential-free status JSON in CI
items.acceptanceSeed: A temporary dummy auth plus offline/mock provider exercises the real normalization path.

items.title: Block external network in fixture tests
items.acceptanceSeed: Dummy or real secrets cannot reach ChatGPT from the test suite.

items.title: Test missing auth and expired-token failures
items.acceptanceSeed: CI validates failure schemas as well as a happy-path usage snapshot.

items.title: Run typecheck/lint/unit/integration gates
items.acceptanceSeed: Commands fail the job on actual errors rather than relying on final echo output.

items.title: Run update failure-injection tests
items.acceptanceSeed: Hash, download, archive, lock, activation and rollback failures are covered.

items.title: Run clean link/pack/install tests
items.acceptanceSeed: The produced CLI installs and runs outside the developer checkout without GUI dependencies.

items.title: Run all claimed OS/architecture jobs
items.acceptanceSeed: Missing runners remain visible; a Windows-only local result is not cross-platform acceptance.

items.title: Inspect real workflow conclusions
items.acceptanceSeed: Written, queued, skipped, failed and passed workflows are distinguished.

items.title: Keep model tests opt-in
items.acceptanceSeed: No routine CI job submits paid/token-consuming coding or Web requests.

items.title: Preserve GUI regression evidence
items.acceptanceSeed: Migration acceptance runs the existing GUI native/reference gates rather than only CLI tests.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Create a separate CLI requirement catalog
items.acceptanceSeed: Every original request maps to stable CLI IDs without importing GUI progress credit.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Expand the atomic seed inventory
items.acceptanceSeed: Each item receives verbose scope, acceptance, dependencies, paths and test evidence.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Keep conditional and blocked requirements visible
items.acceptanceSeed: Web/size/auth/platform conflicts cannot disappear from the denominator without approved scope change.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Use evidence-backed stage credit
items.acceptanceSeed: 0/10/40/65/85/100 stage semantics have explicit acceptance criteria.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Freeze baseline weights per task
items.acceptanceSeed: Weights cannot be adjusted just to increase the reported overall percentage.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Compute weighted overall CLI maturity
items.acceptanceSeed: Math is deterministic and tested; requirement count is not treated as effort.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Show independent GUI and CLI README bars
items.acceptanceSeed: MTerm-GUI README links its GUI bar/roadmap and MTerm-CLI README links its CLI bar/roadmap; both link the sibling product.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Preserve GUI percentage during repository export
items.acceptanceSeed: Repository export alone confers no additional GUI implementation credit.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Render color-coded per-item and area bars
items.acceptanceSeed: Accessible text accompanies local SVG colors; blockers retain earned credit.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Publish a verbose numbered feature table
items.acceptanceSeed: Every CLI requirement has percentage, remaining effort, ETA state, evidence and blocker.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Provide an offline searchable dashboard
items.acceptanceSeed: Search/status/component filters work without external badge or runtime services.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Keep ETA assumptions honest
items.acceptanceSeed: Calendar dates require an actual capacity/dependency basis; otherwise use Unscheduled.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Record reviewed source/catalog fingerprints
items.acceptanceSeed: Changing CLI source, pins or reviewed settings invalidates stale assessments.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Test exported GUI fingerprint coverage
items.acceptanceSeed: Changes under MTerm-GUI/native and its GUI reference paths are still caught.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Enforce metrics at relevant gates
items.acceptanceSeed: Build/package/CI publication checks reject stale reviews rather than silently regenerating credit.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Update contributor entry points in both repositories
items.acceptanceSeed: Each repository's AGENTS, templates and existing vendor pointers require metrics maintenance.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Separate rendering from review approval
items.acceptanceSeed: A render command cannot satisfy the explicit human/AI assessment requirement.

items.section: CLI roadmap, progress bars and governance
items.title: Retain complete cross-repository source-project traceability
items.acceptanceSeed: GUI lineage and the CLI’s three upstream licenses/features remain documented independently.

items.title: Record actual contributor identity
items.acceptanceSeed: Provider/model is self-reported accurately or unknown; no invented provenance.

items.title: Preserve original authorship
items.acceptanceSeed: Modified upstream/GUI files retain their origin and receive scoped change references.

items.title: Explain non-obvious invariants in comments
items.acceptanceSeed: Ownership, credential boundaries, units and lifecycle assumptions are visible near relevant code.

items.title: Write durable task change records
items.acceptanceSeed: UTC/base SHA/IDs/files/tests/decisions/limitations/next step are inside the repository.

items.title: Record mandatory roadmap_updates
items.acceptanceSeed: Every source change has a reviewed metric update or a justified no-stage-change review.

items.title: Checkpoint migration and vertical slices
items.acceptanceSeed: Verified bundles/manifests permit recovery without relying on chat memory.

items.title: Resume from observed state
items.acceptanceSeed: Reconnect inspects actual processes/files/logs before repeating a write or install.

items.title: Leave vendor-neutral handoff instructions
items.acceptanceSeed: Another AI company’s model can discover the current source of truth and next task from the repo.

items.title: Prepare a reviewable integration PR
items.acceptanceSeed: Migration, implementation, evidence, generated metrics and upstream decisions are inspectable.

items.title: Reconcile concurrent upstream changes
items.acceptanceSeed: Merge decisions use refreshed remote hashes and avoid overwriting work added during execution.

items.title: Merge with expected-head protection
items.acceptanceSeed: Ordinary repository checks/permissions are respected without force or policy changes.

items.title: Verify the resulting main tree
items.acceptanceSeed: Fetch and compare remote/local state after the successful merge action.

items.title: Select a non-conflicting CLI tag
items.acceptanceSeed: Prefer cli-v0.1.0; a bare v0.1.0 is used only when unused and explicitly scoped.

items.title: Tag only accepted mandatory scope
items.acceptanceSeed: Required unvalidated Web/size/platform behavior blocks a full release claim unless scope is explicitly revised.

items.title: Keep tag and package publication distinct
items.acceptanceSeed: No claim that a Git tag automatically published npm assets, signed binaries or releases.

items.title: Preserve rollback and old branches
items.acceptanceSeed: No destructive history cleanup, tag overwrite or branch deletion is bundled into release.

items.title: Deliver a complete final evidence report
items.acceptanceSeed: Report exact commands, SHAs, size accounting, compatibility, real CI state and known blockers.

items.title: Publish runnable setup/update/rollback documentation
items.acceptanceSeed: A fresh user can install, diagnose, use and recover the CLI without hidden developer context.

items.title: Measure wrapper overhead separately
items.acceptanceSeed: Startup timing excludes remote model reasoning and distinguishes cold/warm environments.

items.title: Measure cached statusline latency
items.acceptanceSeed: The reported timing comes from the real packaged path with a stated environment/sample count.

items.title: Measure each platform installation
items.acceptanceSeed: Disk accounting is performed after extraction, including automatically installed requirements.

items.title: Prove status/help do not start heavyweight helpers
items.acceptanceSeed: Process/fixture tests detect accidental browser, GUI, agent or daemon startup.

items.title: Bound process and log memory
items.acceptanceSeed: Long command output and helper errors do not accumulate without a configured bound.

items.title: Test installed behavior rather than only source execution
items.acceptanceSeed: Packaged/link-installed artifacts pass the same representative command contracts.

items.title: Expose performance regressions honestly
items.acceptanceSeed: Measured regressions remain visible; no “never slows down” or unlike CLI/GUI comparison claims.

items.title: Keep development tooling out of runtime
items.acceptanceSeed: Build/test/progress generation dependencies are excluded from installed CLI operation where possible.
